subject: Music
generalObjectives: Appreciate and discuss the foundations of Music fairly and critically.
Identify the features of the music of different periods through written and aural analysis.
Investigate Western and African music theory, history, peoples, forms and medium of performance, including instrumentation.
Recognise the influence of socio-cultural and technological factors, including computer software applications, on the lives and music of musicians.
Acquire a sound musical basis for further learning at the tertiary level.

topics.title: The Staff
subtopics: G clef (treble), C clef (alto, tenor, etc.) and F clef (bass).
objectives: Identify all the components of the staff and their uses.

topics.title: Music Notes and Rests
subtopics: Corresponding values of notes and rests.
objectives: Determine the relative duration of different notes and rests and their applications.

topics.title: Time Signature
objectives: Interpret varied rhythmic patterns.
Group and bar unbarred passages correctly.

topics.title: Key Signatures and Scales
subtopics: Technical names of the various degrees of the scale.
Diatonic minor scales: natural, harmonic and melodic.
Determination of the key of a piece of music with or without a key signature, not exceeding two sharps and two flats.
objectives: Ascertain the names of the various degrees of diatonic scales and keys.
Identify simple scale passages with or without a key signature.
Differentiate between diatonic and chromatic scales.

topics.title: Keyboard Setting, Enharmonic Equivalents and Accidentals
objectives: Identify the names of the white and black keys and their relationships, for example, C-sharp and B-double-sharp.
State the functions of accidentals.

topics.title: Intervals
subtopics: Recognition of diatonic and chromatic intervals.
Perfect unison, perfect fourth, perfect fifth and perfect octave.
Major and minor seconds, thirds, sixths and sevenths.
objectives: Determine different qualities of melodic and harmonic intervals and their inversions.

topics.title: Musical Terms, Signs and Abbreviations
objectives: Interpret simple musical terms, signs and abbreviations.

topics.title: Transcription and Transposition
subtopics: Transcription of music from staff notation into tonic solfa notation and vice versa.
Transposition using the treble (G) and bass (F) staves, not exceeding two sharps and two flats.
objectives: Read music in a given notation, both staff and solfa notation.
Rewrite a music passage on a given stave.
Transcribe from staff notation to solfa notation.

topics.title: Triads and Their Inversions
subtopics: Triads and their inversions in major and minor keys, not exceeding two sharps and two flats.
Chord indications: major triads represented by capital Roman numerals, such as I.
Minor triads represented by small Roman numerals, such as ii.
Diminished triads represented by small Roman numerals with a degree sign, such as vii°.
Augmented triads represented by capital Roman numerals with a plus sign, such as III+.
In major scales, major triads are I, IV and V; minor triads are ii, iii and vi; the diminished triad is vii°.
In harmonic minor scales, minor triads are i and iv; major triads are V and VI; diminished triads are ii° and vii°; the augmented triad is III+.
Primary triads are I, IV and V in major scales, and i, iv and V in harmonic minor scales.
objectives: Identify triads and their inversions in major and minor keys.
Compare types of triads.
Determine the uses of triads.

topics.title: Basic Chord Progressions and Dominant Seventh Chord
subtopics: Basic chord progressions in four-part vocal style (SATB) in major keys, not exceeding two sharps and two flats.
Dominant seventh chord in root position only.
objectives: Determine basic chord progressions in a musical passage.
Recognise the dominant seventh chord.

topics.title: Kinds of Motion
objectives: Identify the various kinds of motion in a musical passage.
Differentiate between the various kinds of motion.

topics.title: Cadences
subtopics: Cadences in major keys, not exceeding two sharps and two flats.
Interrupted, deceptive, evaded or surprise cadence.
objectives: Identify the various types of cadences in a musical score.
Analyse the types of cadences and their resolutions.

topics.title: Non-Harmonic Tones and Non-Chord Tones
subtopics: Identification and application of non-harmonic tones and non-chord tones.
objectives: Relate harmonic or non-harmonic tones to the chords with which they are associated.

topics.title: Modulation
subtopics: Simple diatonic modulations using a single melodic line.
Modulation from any given major key, not exceeding two sharps and two flats, to closely related keys.
objectives: Determine the key of a given melody and its modulation.

topics.title: Elementary Composition
subtopics: Setting words to a written melody.
Recognition of suitable answers to given musical phrases.
objectives: Identify suitable melodies for given words and compatible, balanced or contrasting phrases.
Identify the basic rules of two-part writing and counterpoint.

sections.sectionTitle: Section C: History and Literature of African Music

topics.title: Nigerian Folksongs: Types, Forms and Characteristics
subtopics: Types of folksongs: cradle songs, folk tales, games, war songs, satirical songs, dirges or funeral songs, historical songs, praise songs and work songs.
Forms: call and response, strophic, through-composed and antiphony.
Vocal styles: recitative, yodelling, ululation, incantation, heaving, whistling and nasalisation.
Scales and modes: tritonic, tetratonic, pentatonic and hexatonic.
Metre and rhythm: metric and non-metric, polymetric, cross-rhythm, syncopation, hemiola and polyrhythm.
objectives: Identify various folksongs and their types.
Define and compare their forms and features.
Mention characteristic features of vocal, scale and rhythmic styles in African music.

topics.title: Nigerian Traditional Music, Festivals, Dances and Other Arts
subtopics: Features and forms of Nigerian traditional music and other arts.
Festivals: Osun, Ifa, Ogun, Ekpo, Ofala, Iri ji (New Yam Festival), Ovia Osese, Mmanwu (Masquerade), Ila-Oso, Argungu Fishing Festival, Eyo or Adamu Orisa and Gelede.
Dances and other arts: social, ritual and ceremonial forms.
Examples: Masquerade, Koroso, Atilogwu, Ikperikpe (war dance), Egedeege, Kwaghir, Agbon, Nkwa Umuagbogho, Bata, Bori, Swange, Dundun, Kokoma, Abigbo and Okonko.
objectives: Analyse the features and forms of Nigerian traditional music and the arts.
Differentiate between types of festivals and dances and identify their origins.
Identify the relationship between music, dance and drama in African festivals.

topics.title: Nigerian Traditional Musical Instruments
subtopics: Classification of Nigerian traditional musical instruments.
Aerophones: kakaki, algaita, sarewa, pedete, obati, farai, kaho, imar, mongom, taluk, damalgo, oja, opi, pipilo, udu, nnuk, ofiom, akpele, ekutu, teremagbe, ayeta-ode and odikakora.
Chordophones: goge, kukuma, komo, kwamsa, kuntigi, lasha, molo, garaya, gurmi, une, ubo-akwara and goje.
Idiophones: kundung, karawa, shantu, oyo, ichaka, ogene, aja, ekpili, ekwe, udu, ikoro, ngedegwu, okpokoro, ekere, mgbiligba, alo, ubo-aka, sekere, agogo, agidigbo, alọ, oma, aro, ukuse and eromwon.
Membranophones: ganga, tambari, taushi, banga, balle, kuntuku, kalangu, gangan-noma, tandu, igba, nsing, ban yogume, emoba, ipese, igbin, bata, bembe, gudugudu, kanango, dundun and gangan.
objectives: Identify the characteristic features of the classes of musical instruments.
Classify instruments into their categories.
Trace the origins of the instruments.

topics.title: African Traditional Musicians
subtopics: Lives and music of Nigerian traditional musicians.

Northern Nigerian musicians: Sani Sabulu, Sani Dan Indo, Hassan Wayam, Barmani Coge, Danlami Nasarawa, Garba Super, Dankwairo, Aminu Mai Asharalle, Shehu Ajilo, Dan Maraya Jos, Dan Alalo, Mamman Shata and Haruna Uji.
Eastern Nigerian musicians: Ezigbo Obiligbo, Seven-Seven, Morocco Maduka, Okechukwu Nwatu, Mike Ejeagha and Afam Ogbuotobo.
Western Nigerian musicians: Kokoro (the blind minstrel), Anikura, Tunde Alao, Olanrewaju Adepoju, Ademola Onibonokuta, Elemure Ogunyemi and Comfort Omoge.
Other African traditional musicians: Vinoko Akpalu, Daniel Amponsah (Koo Nimo), Efua Basa and Kwaa Mensah.
objectives: Identify the different groups to which the musicians belong.
Trace their biographies.
Mention their musical styles.
Assess their contributions to the music industry.

topics.title: Evolution and Development of African Popular Music
objectives: Differentiate one musical genre from another.
Examine the influence of the genres on society.

subtopics: Nigerian art musicians: W. W. C. Echezona, Laz Ekwueme, Sam Akpabot, Ikoli Harcourt Whyte, Joshua Uzoigwe, Mosun Omibiyi-Obidike, Tunji Vidal, Ademola Adegbite, Yemi Olaniyan, Ayo Bankole, Akin Euba, Sam Ojukwu, A. K. sections.sectionTitle: Section D: History and Literature of Western Music

topics.title: Historical Development of Western Music
objectives: Identify the various periods and their dates from the Medieval period to the 20th century.
Trace the stages of the development of Western musical practice from the Medieval period to the end of the 20th century.

topics.title: Western Music Composers
objectives: Identify the composers.
Assess their contributions.

topics.title: Music Forms and Media
subtopics: Musical forms: binary, ternary, rondo, sonata allegro, dance suite, canon, free fantasia and theme and variation.
Orchestral and band instruments and their classifications.
The human voice: types, ranges and qualities.
Keyboard instruments: organ, piano and electronic keyboard.
Other instruments: ukulele, banjo, guitar, mandolin, harp, accordion, xylophone and marimba.
Computer music technology and software: Finale, Sibelius, Cubase, Reason and Sound Forge Nero.
Introduction to artificial intelligence in music technology: meaning, evolutionary trend and historical background.
Types and applications of AI tools in music composition.
objectives: Identify the general forms and various types of instruments in Western music.
Relate music to modern technology.
Assess the contributions of artificial intelligence to music.

subtopics: Overview of Black musicians, including composers and performers, in the diaspora.

Mighty Sparrow, James Brown, Bob Marley, Michael Jackson, Stevie Wonder, Lionel Richie, R. Kelly, Lauryn Hill, Kirk Franklin, Tupac Shakur, Shabba Ranks, Quincy Jones, Boyz II Men, Sean Paul, Janet Jackson, Whitney Houston, Beyoncé, Brandy, Usher, Kevin Lyttle, Bobby Brown, MC Hammer, LL Cool J, Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Mary J. Blige, Jay-Z, Chris Brown, Bruno Mars, Ne-Yo, Rihanna, Louis Armstrong, Jimmy Cliff and Diana Ross.

Assess their individual musical influences on global society.

topics.title: Musical Genres and Their Origins
objectives: Identify the various forms of musical genres.
Trace the origins of the musical genres.

subtopics: The spirit of nationalism in Nigerian music.
First National Anthem, Nigeria We Hail Thee — Frances Brenda (1960–1978), as listed in the source.
